sections.html:
Forty minutes southwest of Salt Lake City, on the western slope of the Oquirrh Mountains at 4,915 feet, Tooele is the seat of Tooele County. The valley is a separate world from the Salt Lake Valley next door, with its own schools, history and tax office. The county covers 6,923 square miles, and most towns lie in the wide valley between the Oquirrh Mountains and the Onaqui and Stansbury ranges.

Tooele keeps growing. The city counted 35,742 people in 2020 and is estimated at 42,270 on July 1, 2025. Older neighborhoods such as New Town, built for smelter workers, sit beside newer areas that have added thousands of residents since 2020.

That median spans the entire city, so age and condition can put your own house above or below it.

Most trips to the capital use State Route 36 to Interstate 80, and that junction jams. It is the first exit for westbound drivers on I-80, and a storm or crash can back it up for hours.

State Route 179, the Midvalley Highway, opened October 30, 2021. About 4.5 miles long, it ties SR-138 to I-80, so people heading to Erda and Grantsville can skip SR-36. UDOT expected it to cut traffic at the I-80 and SR-36 interchange by 15% to 20%, or about 6,000 to 8,000 vehicles a day. It opened with a single lane each way, and more lanes are planned with no date set.

The county grew 25% between 2010 and 2020, fifth-fastest among Utah counties and well above the 18.4% statewide rate. If you commute, state the drive time in your listing, because buyers will ask.

Work here spans mining, industry, defense and government. Kennecott Utah Copper operates the Bingham Canyon Mine on the far side of the Oquirrh Mountains, while EnergySolutions and US Magnesium work west of the valley. Former Army buildings at Tooele Industrial Depot now house manufacturing, warehousing and offices. Federal, state and county agencies employ a good share of residents too.

Summers are hot and winters cold. An average year brings about 18.44 inches of precipitation and 75.3 inches of snow, and temperatures have ranged from 106 degrees to minus 16 degrees.

That much snow puts weight on roofs, gutters and heating systems. Before listing, inspect attic insulation and look for ice damming, and keep records of any roof work.

The county school district has its headquarters in Tooele, and 8 of its 16 elementary schools, 2 of 3 junior highs and 2 of 5 high schools (Tooele High and Blue Peak) are inside the city. The city is also home to a regional Utah State University campus and the Tooele Applied Technology College. Families wanting alternatives can look at Saint Marguerite Catholic School and Scholar Academy Charter School.

Under Utah Code 59-2-1331, the county wants payment by November 30. Taxes still unpaid after that carry a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater. A primary residence is 45% exempt, up to one acre, and the title company divides the current year's bill at closing.

A Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Change goes out at the end of July. You can appeal within 45 days of receiving it, or by September 15. Saying that taxes are too high is not a basis for appeal. The assessor takes four kinds of evidence:

  • Sales of comparable properties before January 1 that sold for less than your value.
  • Your own purchase before January 1, shown with a settlement statement. Short sales, bank-owned and foreclosure sales generally need an appraisal.
  • An appraisal with an effective date within the year.
  • A written statement of a factual error, such as wrong square footage or garage type.

You can look at your property card in person Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Card details are available in person only.

Many sales here come from estates. As an heir, start with who has the legal authority to sign, and collect the papers that show it. Walk the house and decide what stays, what goes and who gets it. Then ask the county for the current tax status so nothing surprises you at the closing table.

A house left empty may have put-off maintenance, an aging roof or furnace, or leftover belongings no one wants. A cash buyer prices all of that in, so clearing out, fixing and staging are not required before you hear a number.

sections.h2: Older homes and what buyers check
sections.html:
Around older streets like New Town, inspectors study roofs, windows, plumbing and wiring. In newer subdivisions the focus shifts to drainage and finishes. A buyer with a mortgage will probably send a repair request after the inspection, and selling as is spares you that negotiation.

In any sale, three kinds of records help: dates for the roof and furnace, permit papers for any addition and receipts for recent work. Together they show a buyer that someone looked after the house, and they save time during the title and offer stages. Keep them in one folder.

sections.h2: What a cash sale offers a Tooele seller
sections.html:
People sell for many reasons, and a cash sale fits when you would rather not repair the house, handle showings or wait on a loan. We buy Tooele houses as is, whether they need maintenance, have tenants or belong to an unsettled estate. You get an offer and choose whether to take it.

A title company runs the closing, pays any back taxes or mortgage from your proceeds and records the deed with the county. Before requesting an offer, gather your valuation notice, the mortgage payoff amount, any lease if the house is rented and the dates of the roof and heating system.

faqs.q: How many people live in Tooele, Utah?
faqs.a: About 42,270 by the July 1, 2025 estimate, compared with 35,742 in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Tooele, Utah?
faqs.a: $381,400 is the survey median for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. It covers the whole city, so your house may land higher or lower.

faqs.q: When must I appeal a Tooele County valuation?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of receiving the notice, or by September 15. The county mails notices at the end of July.

faqs.q: How far is Tooele from Salt Lake City?
faqs.a: Roughly 40 minutes southwest. Drivers mostly take State Route 36 to Interstate 80, and the Midvalley Highway (SR-179), opened in 2021, eases pressure on that interchange.

faqs.q: Will you buy a Tooele house that needs repairs or has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy as is, so nothing has to be fixed, cleared out or staged, and you can decline the offer at no cost.
